key_insight: lPINN shifts most learning offline by pretraining nonlinear basis functions, then solves new PDE instances online with only a final linear optimization under physics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This can greatly cut inference time for forward and inverse physics problems while preserving accuracy, making PINNs more practical for repeated solves and parameter estimation.
method: Train continuous neural basis functions offline on an ensemble of numerical solutions.
Pretrain using solution data plus derivatives or physics residuals to make the basis operator-compatible.
Freeze the basis online and fit only the final linear layer by minimizing PDE residuals and any IC/BC/observation terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower errors than vanilla PINNs and online speedups from about 10x to over 1000x, especially with sparse residual or measurement data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the offline training ensemble, so poor basis coverage may limit generalization to new regimes.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
